analysis: The PR changes only documentation and a CI test. In docs/developer/build.md (head lines 437-454) it updates the pinned watchdog commit reference from 31236c54 to d6d257c2 and clarifies the stranded-run semantics. It states that timing is measured from job creation, that a single stranded shard is rescued, and that payer concurrency waits can look stranded. It also advises setting DARKBLOOM_WATCHDOG_MINUTES above such waits. The other build.md units (lines 1-480, 481-980) show no changed ranges and were reviewed only as context. In scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py the comment pin is updated (line 132) and a new regression assertion (about lines 949-953) forbids passing run/job listings to jq as `--arg`/`--argjson` arguments, to avoid 'Argument list too long'. No provider code, wire protocol, keys, attestation, cache storage, or authorization behavior changes, so none of the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 provider assets (A-001 through A-018) are touched. The prefix-cache threat T-041 was supplied in the canonical context but is not affected. The watchdog token scope (actions: write, checks: write) is unchanged in the documentation. Remaining limit: the actual workflow file .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml and darkbloom-route.yml were not in this batch, so the claim that the copied watchdog matches d6d257c2 and that the jq-argument change is implemented was not verified. It is CI tooling outside the threat model's provider scope, and no security conclusion depends on it.
